title: observability: token-level cost & latency dashboard + alert tuning for KV cache metrics
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds token-level KV cache cost and latency dashboards, refines alert thresholds to reduce noisy incidents; no behavioral changes to runtime.
body:
Context: Our recent Dedicated customers reported noisy KV cache-related alerts and lacked visibility into per-token cost breakdowns for long-running chat sessions. This PR adds token-level cost and latency dashboards for KV cache operations, enriches spans with KV operation metadata, and tunes alert thresholds to reduce false positives while keeping SLO coverage.

Motivation: Reduce on-call noise and give platform teams a clear, per-route/unit economics view of KV cache impact on per-token latency and cost. This enables smarter routing and batching recommendations in Redwood Optimize.

What I changed (high level):
- New Grafana dashboard JSON for token-level KV cache cost/latency (observability/dashboards/token_kv_cost_latency.jsonnet).
- Instrumentation: add kvcache latency/cost histograms and enrich tracing spans with kvcache_hit/miss tags (telemetry/metrics/kvcache_metrics.go, agent/tracing/span_enrichment.go).
- Alerts: tuned alert rules to use p95/p99 token-latency buckets and cost-per-token rolling windows, added suppression windows for rollout periods (alerts/alert_rules.yaml).
- Docs: token-level metrics guide and dashboard walkthrough (docs/observability/token-level-metrics.md).
- Helm values: optional dashboard toggle and increased scrape interval defaults for kvcache metrics (charts/observability/values.yaml).
- Tests: unit & integration tests for metrics export and dashboard generation (tests/observability/test_kv_metrics.py).

Checklist:
- [x] Instrumented metrics exported (histograms & counters)
- [x] Traces enriched with KV metadata for easier root-cause analysis
- [x] Dashboard panels for cost-per-token, latency-by-token, hit/miss ratio, hot-key detection
- [x] Alerts tuned to p95/p99 and validated under load in perf-canary
- [x] Docs updated and example queries included

Commits:
- a1f4d3e: add token-level kvcache histograms and counters
- b2c9fa7: enrich tracing spans with kvcache metadata and route id
- c3d1b88: generate Grafana dashboard for kvcache token-level cost/latency
- d4e2a99: add alert rule tuning and suppression windows
- e5f3b00: docs + helm toggle + tests

Files changed (high level):
- observability/dashboards/token_kv_cost_latency.jsonnet (new) — dashboard panels, templating by route/model/version
- telemetry/metrics/kvcache_metrics.go (modified) — new histograms: kvcache_request_duration_seconds_bucket, kvcache_cost_tokens_total, labels: route_id, model, shard
- agent/tracing/span_enrichment.go (modified) — attach kvcache.hit/kvcache.miss and key_id (hashed) to spans
- alerts/alert_rules.yaml (modified) — new rules: KVCacheHighTokenLatency (p99), KVCacheCostSpike (5m rolling), KVCacheHotKeyAlert
- docs/observability/token-level-metrics.md (new) — queries, dashboard walkthrough, troubleshooting
- charts/observability/values.yaml (modified) — kvcache.metrics.enabled toggle and scrape defaults
- tests/observability/test_kv_metrics.py (new) — unit tests for histogram creation and prometheus exposition

Review summary / conversation highlights:
- Kenji Tanaka (2026-02-13): "Great work on the dashboard layout. A couple nits: please reduce cardinality on the route_id label and hash key_id before attaching to spans to avoid PII leakage."
- Aisha Patel (2026-02-13): "Agree on hashing. Updated span_enrichment to hash key IDs and added config toggle for route_id cardinality (off by default for high-cardinality routes)."
- Maya Chen (2026-02-14): "Alert thresholds look reasonable. Can we add an evaluation run against perf-canary 2026-02-15 to ensure we don't miss regressions on p99?"
- Aisha Patel (2026-02-15): "Ran perf-canary; attached summary in CI artifacts. p99 increase matched expected baseline for bursty workloads, adjusted thresholds down 10% to minimize missed regressions."
- Luca Rossi (2026-02-16): "Tests look good; left one minor comment about metric naming consistency."
- Aisha Patel (2026-02-16): "Fixed metric name to follow telemetry conventions and updated tests."
- Kenji Tanaka (2026-02-17): "Approved after the naming fix and perf validation."

CI / Checks:
- CI / unit-tests: pass (all telemetry unit tests, 98% coverage for new files)
- CI / e2e-observability: pass (deployed dashboards to staging, queries validated)
- CI / perf-canary: pass (ran 3 canary runs; attached durations and cost deltas)
- CI / lint: pass (go fmt, staticcheck)

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main. Merge commit: 9f7b2c3d (squash) by Aisha Patel. No follow-up migrations required.

Notes / follow-ups:
- Ops: will monitor noisy-alerts@redwood for 72 hours and revert thresholds if >3 noisy incidents observed.
- Product: Redwood Optimize team will consume the new cost-per-token metric in next iteration to recommend batching/quantization changes.

If anything else is needed for release notes or to back out quickly, ping me in #observability.
